Content:
That doesn't seem like very much gold.  70ftx70ftx70ft isn't tiny, per se, but ALL the gold on Earth?  Or just all the gold we've mined and purified?

According to Google AI:

The total mass of gold in the Earth's crust is \(1.108\times 10^{11}\) metric tons.

To find the volume, use the density of gold, which is approximately 19.32 metric tons per cubic meter. 

The formula for volume (V) is mass (M) divided by density (\(\rho \)). \(V=\frac{M}{\rho }\)\(V=\frac{1.108\times 10^{11}\text{\ t}}{19.32\text{\ t/m}^{3}}\)\(V\approx 5.735\times 10^{9}\text{\ m}^{3}\)

Calculate the side length of the cube The volume of a cube is given by the formula \(V=s^{3}\), where \(s\) is the side length. 

To find the side length, calculate the cube root of the volume. \(s=\sqrt[3]{V}\)\(s=\sqrt[3]{5.735\times 10^{9}\text{\ m}^{3}}\)\(s\approx 1,789.7\text{\ m}\)

Answer: The cube of gold would have a side length of approximately 1,790 meters (or 1.79 kilometers).
